notes: 23 distinct original AQA-style Maths questions with independently graded method steps.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A sixth form contains 720 Year 12 and 480 Year 13 students. A researcher requires a proportionate stratified random sample of 100. Find each year group's allocation and explain how to select students fairly.
markPoints: Select numbered pupils using independent random numbers without replacement within each year group.
questions.modelAnswer: Total population is 1200. Year 12 allocation is 100×720/1200=60. Year 13 allocation is 100×480/1200=40. Select numbered pupils using independent random numbers without replacement within each year group.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Grouped travel times (minutes) have frequencies 0–10: 6, 10–20: 12, 20–40: 16, and 40–60: 6. Calculate histogram frequency densities and estimate the mean. State a limitation of the estimate.
markPoints: Estimated mean is 990/40=24.75 min; within-class values are unknown.
questions.modelAnswer: Class widths are 10, 10, 20 and 20. Frequency densities are 0.6, 1.2, 0.8 and 0.3. Midpoint weighted sum is 5×6+15×12+30×16+50×6=990. Estimated mean is 990/40=24.75 min; within-class values are unknown.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A vehicle accelerates uniformly from 36 km h⁻¹ to 90 km h⁻¹ in 10 s. Find its acceleration and displacement in SI units, stating the speed conversion.
markPoints: Divide km h⁻¹ speeds by 3.6: u=10 and v=25 m s⁻¹.
Mean velocity over uniform acceleration is (10+25)/2=17.5 m s⁻¹.
questions.modelAnswer: Divide km h⁻¹ speeds by 3.6: u=10 and v=25 m s⁻¹. Acceleration a=(25−10)/10=1.5 m s⁻². Mean velocity over uniform acceleration is (10+25)/2=17.5 m s⁻¹. Displacement s=17.5×10=175 m.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: P(A)=0.60, P(B)=0.50 and P(A∩B)=0.25. Find P(A∪B), find P(A|B), and decide with a calculation whether A and B are independent.
markPoints: Since P(A)P(B)=0.30≠0.25, events are not independent.
questions.modelAnswer: P(A∪B)=0.60+0.50−0.25. Union probability is 0.85. Conditional probability P(A|B)=0.25/0.50=0.50. Since P(A)P(B)=0.30≠0.25, events are not independent.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: An arithmetic sequence has third term 17 and eighth term 42. Determine its first term, common difference and sum of the first 20 terms.
questions.modelAnswer: Write a+2d=17 and a+7d=42. Subtract to obtain 5d=25, giving d=5. First term a=17−10=7. S20=10[2×7+19×5]=1090.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A sector has radius 9 cm and arc length 12 cm. Calculate its angle in radians and its area. Explain why using degrees directly in A=½r²θ would be incorrect.
markPoints: Arc length s=rθ gives θ=12/9=4/3 rad.
The formula requires radians because θ is the dimensionless arc-length-to-radius ratio.
questions.modelAnswer: Arc length s=rθ gives θ=12/9=4/3 rad. Use sector area A=½r²θ. A=½×81×(4/3)=54 cm². The formula requires radians because θ is the dimensionless arc-length-to-radius ratio.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Let f(x)=3x−2 and g(x)=x²+1. Find f(g(2)), g(f(2)), the inverse of f and the domain and range of the inverse when f acts on all real numbers.
markPoints: The inverse has domain and range both equal to the real numbers.
questions.modelAnswer: f(g(2))=f(5)=13. g(f(2))=g(4)=17. Inverse function f⁻¹(x)=(x+2)/3. The inverse has domain and range both equal to the real numbers.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Solve |2x−3|=x+1 for real x by considering both signs of the modulus expression. State the condition for each case and show that every proposed solution satisfies the original equation.
markPoints: First note right side x+1 must be non-negative.
Both candidates satisfy their branch conditions and original equation.
questions.modelAnswer: First note right side x+1 must be non-negative. If 2x−3≥0 then 2x−3=x+1, giving x=4. If 2x−3<0 then 3−2x=x+1, giving x=2/3. Both candidates satisfy their branch conditions and original equation.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Show that (1−cos²x)/(sin x cos x)=tan x where defined, and identify excluded values for 0≤x<2π.
markPoints: Cancel one sin x factor to obtain sin x/cos x.
The original denominator is zero at 0, π/2, π and 3π/2.
questions.modelAnswer: Use the identity 1−cos²x=sin²x. Cancel one sin x factor to obtain sin x/cos x. Use tan x=sin x/cos x. The original denominator is zero at 0, π/2, π and 3π/2.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A fountain model has height h(t)=12t−4t² metres, t≥0. Determine when its height is greatest, the height and why the stationary point is a maximum.
markPoints: Set derivative to zero: t=1.5 s.
Second derivative −8 is negative, confirming a maximum.
questions.modelAnswer: Differentiate h'(t)=12−8t. Set derivative to zero: t=1.5 s. Height h(1.5)=18−9=9 m. Second derivative −8 is negative, confirming a maximum.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Find the total finite region enclosed by the curve y=6x−x² and the x-axis, stating the integration limits and showing the evaluation.
markPoints: Curve meets the axis where x(6−x)=0, so x=0 and x=6.
questions.modelAnswer: Curve meets the axis where x(6−x)=0, so x=0 and x=6. Area=∫₀⁶(6x−x²)dx. Antiderivative is 3x²−x³/3. Evaluate to 108−72=36 square units.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Prove algebraically that the difference between the squares of two consecutive integers is always odd.
markPoints: Represent consecutive integers by n and n+1 for integer n.
Since 2n is even for every integer n, 2n+1 is odd.
questions.modelAnswer: Represent consecutive integers by n and n+1 for integer n. Difference is (n+1)²−n². Simplifies to 2n+1. Since 2n is even for every integer n, 2n+1 is odd.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Express (5x+7)/[(x+1)(x+3)] in partial fractions, then obtain its indefinite integral.
questions.modelAnswer: Set expression equal to A/(x+1)+B/(x+3). Coefficients give A+B=5 and 3A+B=7. Solve A=1 and B=4. Integral is ln|x+1|+4ln|x+3|+C.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A curve has parameters x=t²+1 and y=t³−2t. Find dy/dx when t=2 and the equation of the tangent at the corresponding point.
markPoints: At t=2 the gradient is 5/2 and coordinates are (5,4).
questions.modelAnswer: dx/dt=2t and dy/dt=3t²−2. dy/dx=(3t²−2)/(2t). At t=2 the gradient is 5/2 and coordinates are (5,4). Tangent is y−4=(5/2)(x−5).

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Three points have position vectors A=(1,2,−1), B=(4,0,3), C=(7,−2,7). Show they are collinear and find AB:BC.
markPoints: The displacement vectors are equal and non-zero, proving collinearity.
Their lengths are equal, so AB:BC=1:1.
questions.modelAnswer: AB=(3,−2,4). BC=(3,−2,4). The displacement vectors are equal and non-zero, proving collinearity. Their lengths are equal, so AB:BC=1:1.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A factory makes components independently with a probability 0.08 of being defective. In a sample of 20, calculate P(exactly two defective) and P(at least one defective).
markPoints: Probability at least one defective is 1−0.92²⁰≈0.811.
questions.modelAnswer: X~Binomial(20,0.08). P(X=2)=C(20,2)×0.08²×0.92¹⁸≈0.271. P(X≥1)=1−P(X=0). Probability at least one defective is 1−0.92²⁰≈0.811.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Fill mass X is normally distributed with mean 510 g and standard deviation 9 g. Calculate P(X<495) and the 90th percentile, using Φ(−1.667)=0.0478 and z(0.90)=1.282.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A particle's displacement is s(t)=t³−6t²+9t metres for t≥0. Find all positive times when it is at rest and show whether direction reverses at each time.
markPoints: Stationary times t=1 s and t=3 s.
Velocity changes from positive to negative at 1 and negative to positive at 3, so it reverses at each.
questions.modelAnswer: Differentiate v=3t²−12t+9. Factor v=3(t−1)(t−3). Stationary times t=1 s and t=3 s. Velocity changes from positive to negative at 1 and negative to positive at 3, so it reverses at each.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A 2.5 kg block slides across a rough horizontal table under an 18 N horizontal applied force. Opposing friction remains 5.5 N. Calculate acceleration and displacement from rest after 3.0 s.
markPoints: From Newton's second law a=12.5/2.5=5.0 m s⁻².
questions.modelAnswer: Resultant force is 18−5.5=12.5 N. From Newton's second law a=12.5/2.5=5.0 m s⁻². From rest s=½at². Displacement s=0.5×5×9=22.5 m.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: The concentration C(t)=80e^(−0.18t), with t in hours. Find its half-life and determine when it falls below 15. Explain any inequality sign reversal.
markPoints: After logarithms −0.18t<ln(15/80); dividing by a negative reverses the inequality.
questions.modelAnswer: Half-life is ln2/0.18≈3.85 h. For C<15 require e^(−0.18t)<15/80. After logarithms −0.18t<ln(15/80); dividing by a negative reverses the inequality. Thus t>ln(80/15)/0.18≈9.30 h.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: An object's temperature θ satisfies dθ/dt=−0.12(θ−18), with initial temperature 78°C. Solve for θ(t) and find when it reaches 30°C.
markPoints: For θ=30, t=ln5/0.12≈13.41 in the given time units.
questions.modelAnswer: Separate variables dθ/(θ−18)=−0.12dt. Integrate ln|θ−18|=−0.12t+C. Initial condition gives θ=18+60e^(−0.12t). For θ=30, t=ln5/0.12≈13.41 in the given time units.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Use the trapezium rule with step size 0.5 to estimate the integral of y=x³+1 from x=0 to x=2. Find the exact integral using algebraic integration and state whether the trapezium-rule estimate is an overestimate or underestimate, explaining the shape of the curve.
markPoints: Exact integral [x⁴/4+x] from 0 to 2 equals 6; the estimate is too large because the curve is convex for x>0.
questions.modelAnswer: The ordinates at x=0,0.5,1,1.5,2 are 1,1.125,2,4.375,9. Trapezium rule: T=(0.5/2)[1+2(1.125+2+4.375)+9]. Trapezium estimate T=6.25 square units. Exact integral [x⁴/4+x] from 0 to 2 equals 6; the estimate is too large because the curve is convex for x>0.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: Find every solution to the trigonometric equation 2cos²x−3cosx+1=0 in the interval 0≤x<2π. Give the answers exactly in radians, explaining how you obtain all possible angles.
markPoints: cosx=1 gives x=0; there are three solutions.
questions.modelAnswer: Set u=cosx and factor (2u−1)(u−1)=0. So cosx=1/2 or cosx=1. cosx=1/2 gives x=π/3 and 5π/3. cosx=1 gives x=0; there are three solutions.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: The circle C has equation x²+y²−4x+6y−12=0. The point P(5,1) lies on C. (a) Complete the square to find the centre and radius of C.
questions.modelAnswer: Complete the x-square: x²−4x=(x−2)²−4. Complete the y-square: y²+6y=(y+3)²−9. Obtain (x−2)²+(y+3)²=25, centre (2,−3), radius 5.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: The circle C has equation x²+y²−4x+6y−12=0. The point P(5,1) lies on C. (b) Find the exact equation of the tangent to C at P, giving your answer in the form ax+by=c.
markPoints: Find the radius gradient from (2,−3) to (5,1): (1+3)/(5−2)=4/3.
questions.modelAnswer: Find the radius gradient from (2,−3) to (5,1): (1+3)/(5−2)=4/3. Use the perpendicular tangent gradient −3/4. Use y−1=−3(x−5)/4 to get 3x+4y=19.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A uniform horizontal beam of length 4.0 m is hinged to a wall at its left end O. The beam weighs 60 N, acting at its midpoint. A 100 N load acts vertically downwards 3.0 m from O. A cable at the right-hand end pulls upwards and to the right at 30° above the horizontal. The beam is at rest. (a) Taking moments about O, determine the tension in the cable.
markPoints: Anticlockwise moment is (4.0 T sin30°) N m.
questions.modelAnswer: Anticlockwise moment is (4.0 T sin30°) N m. Clockwise moments total (60×2.0+100×3.0)=420 N m. Equating moments gives T=210 N.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: A uniform horizontal beam of length 4.0 m is hinged to a wall at its left end O. The beam weighs 60 N, acting at its midpoint. A 100 N load acts vertically downwards 3.0 m from O. A cable at the right-hand end pulls upwards and to the right at 30° above the horizontal. The beam is at rest. (b) Calculate the horizontal and vertical components of the hinge reaction at O and hence its magnitude. State the reaction directions.
markPoints: Horizontal equilibrium gives the hinge reaction 210cos30°=182 N to the left.
Vertical equilibrium gives reaction 160−210sin30°=55 N upwards.
questions.modelAnswer: Horizontal equilibrium gives the hinge reaction 210cos30°=182 N to the left. Vertical equilibrium gives reaction 160−210sin30°=55 N upwards. Resultant hinge force √(182²+55²)≈190 N.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: The function f(x)=(1+2x)⁻¹ᐟ² is expanded as a binomial series about x=0. (a) Find the first three non-zero terms, in ascending powers of x.
questions.modelAnswer: Use (1+u)^n=1+nu+[n(n−1)/2]u²+... with n=−1/2 and u=2x. Linear term is (−1/2)(2x)=−x. Quadratic term is [((−1/2)(−3/2))/2](2x)²=3x²/2, so f(x)≈1−x+3x²/2.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.question: Independent practice
questions.prompt: The function f(x)=(1+2x)⁻¹ᐟ² is expanded as a binomial series about x=0. (b) Use the first three non-zero terms of the binomial expansion to estimate f(0.05), and state the interval of x over which the full expansion converges.
questions.modelAnswer: Substitute x=0.05 in 1−x+3x²/2 to obtain 0.95375. Binomial convergence requires |2x|<1, so −0.5<x<0.5.
